Executive summary

Independent recheck of the WO-05 trusted table confirms all four packages qualify: quality 100, 95, 91 and 88 all clear the 80 floor, and defect counts 3, 1, 3 and 5 sit at or under the ceiling, with P4 exactly at five. On the shared acceptance basis, measured energy ranks P2 15, P3 24, P1 44 and P4 64 kWh, so P2 is the client-correct selection with successive gaps of 9, 20 and 20 kWh and a 49 kWh spread. The policy requires quality at least 80 and raw defects at most 5. Recomputed from the trusted table: P1 quality 100 (margin +20), P2 95 (+15), P3 91 (+11), P4 88 (+8) — all pass. Defect counts P1 3, P2 1, P3 3, P4 5 — all pass, with P4 exactly on the ceiling and zero spare slots, so one additional measured defect would disqualify it. Qualification is binary and no candidate is a near-miss at either screen. Because the energy minimum is unique and strict, no candidate-ID tie-break can arise in this round.

Energy Ranking and Gap Recompute

All packages deliver the same specified charging output under one identical acceptance test, so the kWh figures are directly comparable. Recomputed ladder: P2 15, P3 24, P1 44, P4 64 kWh. Successive gaps are 9, 20 and 20 kWh; winner-to-last spread 49. Energy-per-quality ratios 0.16, 0.26, 0.44 and 0.73 preserve the same order. A's prose arithmetic checks out this round, but the delivered pixel diagnostics do not let me confirm its figure's bar heights, so my own diagram declares a fixed 5 px-per-kWh scale with baseline y=410 for pixel audit.

P2 combines the lowest measured energy with the second-best quality margin (+15) and the largest spare defect capacity (4 slots). P1's +20 margin is the most robust quality buffer, but at 44 kWh it cannot compete on energy. P4's zero spare slots and 64 kWh make it the weakest package on every measured dimension; its raw defect count warrants a direct recheck before any acceptance decision.

Measured facts are limited to one quality index, one raw defect count and one energy figure per candidate, all on the identical output and load basis. P2
